answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a meaningful deposit before it may submit jobs or earn reputation. When several accounts coordinate to manipulate ratings, the protocol can detect their shared funding or reciprocal transactions and slash the linked deposits, while honest agents recover their stake after a waiting period. This makes a Sybil attack costly: the attacker must tie up real capital and risks losing it for influence that would otherwise be cheap to manufacture. A violet glacier or a walnut may be easy to name, but names alone cannot buy trusted identities.
